questions.s: It should be "a miserly man" or "a miser".

questions.q:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

It turned out to be the noisy park party anybody had ever attended.
o: the noisy park party
It turned out to be
questions.s:
The erroneous part is 'the noisy park party'.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
  • Here, 'the noisiest park party' should be used instead of 'the noisy park'.
  • A superlative adjective expresses the extreme or highest degree of quality.
  • We use a superlative adjective to describe the extreme quality of one thing in a group of things. 
  • We should add -er for the comparative and -est for the superlative.
    • Example: Your dog ran the fastest of any dog in the race.
  • If the adjective has a consonant + single vowel + consonant spelling, the final consonant must be doubled before adding the ending.
  • Thus, the correct answer is Option 2.
     

Correct Sentence: It turned out to be the noisiest park party anybody had ever attended.

questions.q: He studied (a) / so hard (b) / he was sure of passing. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: The error is in part (b). The adverb should be 'hardly,' not 'hard,' in this context. Answer: (b). Adverb 'hardly' chahiye, 'hard' galat hai. Jawab: (b).

questions.q:
There are too less space for Naveen to park his car in front of the shop.

[CHSL 14/10/2020 S3]
o: was so few space
was too little space
questions.s: In the given sentence, "too less" is incorrect because "less" is used for uncountable nouns, and "too" already implies a negative comparison. The correct phrase should be "too little," which is used for uncountable nouns like "space.”

questions.q: This is (a) / a very unique (b) / experience. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: The error is in part (b). 'Unique' is absolute; 'very unique' is incorrect. Correct form is 'a unique experience.' Answer: (b). 'Unique' absolute hai, 'very unique' galat hai. Sahi form hai 'a unique experience.' Jawab: (b).

questions.q:
Select the correct superlative degree of comparison for the given sentence.

The money arrived when I (little) expected it.
o: The money arrived when I expected it.
The money arrived when I least expected it.
The money arrived when I less expected it.
The money arrived when I little expected it
questions.s: (b) Explanation:- Ye adjective ki change of degree ka question hai. yhan little ki superlative degree likhni hau jo ki least hoti hai.

questions.q:
He dreams big than his friends.

{CHSL-24 MAY 2022 S2}
questions.s: The correct comparative form of "big" is "bigger." In this sentence, we're comparing the size of dreams between the subject and his friends, so the adjective should be in its comparative form.

questions.q: Both men and women / consider a variety of concerns/ when selecting there outfits. (SSC MTS Tier-01 11/05/23)
questions.s: The possessive pronoun 'their' is needed, not the adverb of place 'there'.

questions.q: The aged require specialized care and attention as he grow older.
o: The aged require specialized
as he grow older
questions.s:
When ‘the’ is used before an adjective, the adjective becomes a plural common noun. It will hence take a plural verb. These adjectives are: Rich, poor, needy, aged, blind, dead, meek, wicked, etc. The correct option is (c) "as he grow older."

The correct sentence should be: "The aged require specialized care and attention as they grow older."

questions.q:
The five first girls/will get the discount/on our merchandise.

[SSC CHSL Tier-01 14/03/23]
o: Will get the discount
questions.s:
When we use both ordinal and cardinal numbers together, the ordinal number (like "first," "second," etc.) comes before the cardinal number (like "five," "ten," etc.).

So, "the first five girls" is the correct order.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Prescription safety glasses provide the ______ tailored protection for individuals with vision correction needs.
questions.s:
It can be noted that the sentence establishes that 'prescription safety glasses' is the ultimate option for people who need vision correction, indicating that the sentence is in superlative degree. Thus, the superlative adjective "finest" is appropriate to indicate the highest degree of tailored protection. "Finer" is comparative, "fine" is positive, and "more finely" is an adverb, which doesn't fit the context.

The complete sentence: Prescription safety glasses provide the finest tailored protection for individuals with vision correction needs.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Note:

· The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compare4.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

questions.s: When comparing two things, the comparative form "smaller" is used instead of the superlative form "smallest."
